title: Extract region-aware networking primitives and upgrade AWS provider to v5.x
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Multiple environments and regions have duplicated, slightly divergent Terraform networking templates (stage/us-west-2, prod/eu-west-1, dedicated/*). Drift and copy-paste changes (tagging, route table associations, NAT config) make small infra changes high-risk and slow. We are also pinned to an older AWS provider (3.x) which prevents using newer resource primitives and causes CI plugin incompatibilities.

Goal: Create a small set of opinionated, region-aware networking primitives (VPC, public/private subnet sets, IGW, NATs, route tables, VPC endpoints, gateway endpoints) as a stable module surface, migrate existing stacks to consume those primitives, and upgrade the AWS provider to v5.x while keeping state intact and minimizing outages.

Why now: Ongoing networking changes for Dedicated capacity and Private deployments expose the duplication. Upgrading provider unlocks improved IAM and endpoint resources and fixes several known plan-time warnings in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new terraform module 'modules/vpc-region' exists with documented inputs/outputs and example usage for multi-account/multi-region.
- All staging and one non-critical production region consume the new module and demonstrate identical plans to the previous templates (modulo expected resource address changes).
- AWS provider bumped to >=5.0 in root modules and CI passes with provider plugin on CI VMs.
- No unplanned resource replacements during migration in the canary region.
- A migration playbook and state commands are committed under docs/infra/vpc-migration.md.
- Rollback procedure verified: ability to switch back to legacy templates within the same deploy window.
- Team signoff from Network/Platform and Security on tagging and endpoint defaults.
technical_notes:
Design decisions and migration approach:
1) Module shape: modules/vpc-region exposes inputs: region, az_count, public_subnet_cidrs, private_subnet_cidrs (map by az), nat_mode (managed/none), enable_vpc_endpoints (list), common_tags. Outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, route_table_ids, endpoints map. Keep resource names deterministic to simplify state moves.
2) Provider strategy: use provider aliases in account/region roots and pass provider configurations into module. Update root provider versions to >=5.0 and pin in versions.tf. Test locally with terraform 1.5 and 1.6 on CI.
3) State migration: perform terraform state mv from legacy addresses to module addresses where possible. For resources that can't be moved cleanly (managed NAT gateways with IPs), import existing resources into new module address. Prepare exact state mv/import commands and run in canary region.
4) CI: add a step that runs 'terraform validate' and 'terraform plan -out' with provider plugin installed. Add smoke apply to a disposable workspace for automated verification.
5) Backwards compatibility: keep a compatibility shim for legacy variables during a 2-week migration window in case teams need extra time.
6) Tagging and policy: standardize tags in module and add an optional map override for org policies.
7) Security: validate that new endpoints and route tables do not widen access scope. Coordinate with Security to run policy-as-code checks after migration.

Operational notes: avoid recreating IGWs/nats during move windows. Prefer using 'terraform state mv' over re-creating resources. Schedule migration during low-traffic windows for production regions.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Discovery spike completed. Catalogued all networking templates across accounts (stage, prod, dedicated). Estimated ~14 distinct TF stacks with 70% reuse potential.
2025-02-22: Architecture review with Platform and Security. Agreed on module surface and tagging defaults. Security requested a VPC endpoint whitelist for S3/Dynamo only by default.

2025-02-26: Prototype module committed (WIP) at modules/vpc-region. First unit tests using terratest added.
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3120
2025-03-01: Provider bump tested locally. CI image initially failed due to older terraform-plugin-sdk on CI runner; upgraded CI runner image and re-ran. CI now picks provider v5.1.0 successfully.
2025-03-03: Began canary migration for staging eu-west-1. Created state move plan and smoke apply in disposable workspace. No unexpected replacements observed in smoke run.
qa_plan: 1) Run 'terraform plan' against a disposable workspace in the canary region and verify zero resource replacements. 2) Apply in canary and run connectivity smoke tests (k8s e2e, internal service pings, S3 access via endpoint). 3) Monitor metrics for NAT throughput and route table errors for 24 hours. 4) After successful canary, schedule batched migrations for remaining regions during maintenance windows.
risk_mitigation:
- Use canary by region before wide rollout.
- Keep legacy templates untouched until module adoption confirmed.
- Documented rollback path using state backups and terraform state mv reverse commands.
- Coordinate with SRE for watch window and quick DNS/route rollback if needed.
notes_for_reviewers: Pay special attention to provider aliases and the proposed variable names for subnet maps; these determine how easy it is for services to consume the module without per-team hacks. Also review the state migration commands in docs/infra/vpc-migration.md for correctness.
next_steps:
- Finalize module outputs and add examples for dedicated capacity accounts.
- Complete migration playbook and schedule prod canary.
- Run comprehensive terraform plan for prod eu-west-1 in a dry-run workspace with SRE present.
- Merge PRs and tag module v1.0.0.
